messages:
olivia: Heads-up — starting ~10:35 UTC we saw a sharp jump in 502/connection resets from inference-edge (us-west-2). App logs show repeated ECONNRESET on outbound calls to model-storage buckets. anyone else seeing this?

mike: looking at cloud metrics now — NAT gateway SNAT port utilization is pegged in us-west-2a, lots of short TCP sessions. charts: https://grafana/redwood/d/egress

infra-oncall: alert: NAT_SNAT_PORT_UTIL >= 99% on nat-gw-3-usw2a :rotating_light:

anya: quick note: model-puller pods are spawning 150 concurrent fetches for checkpoint shards without keepalive. that will blow through ephemeral ports fast.

sam: can we throttle the parallelism in the puller? Also can we flip model fetches to use HTTP keepalive and connection pooling as an immediate fix.

leo: short-term mitigation I'm provisioning an extra NAT gateway in us-west-2b and updating route table for failover. submitting terraform now.

olivia: TY. I'm rolling a canary of a patch that reduces pull concurrency and reuses sockets (adds keepalive). will push logs to #deploy-status.

deploy-bot: deploy started: model-puller v2.14 -> canary (10%)

mike: another lever — enable S3 VPC endpoint for model storage so many pulls skip the NAT entirely. that should cut port demand a lot.

anya: long-term: we should add an internal egress proxy in each AZ to multiplex outbound requests and reuse connections. saved us before on similar incidents.

sam: sample error from pod log: ```ERROR: dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: socket: too many open files``` — that correlates with ephemeral exhaustion + aggressive short-lived connects.

leo: terraform MR: adds nat-gw in 2b, creates S3 gateway endpoint, and increases NAT gw count for the AZ. MR link: https://git.redwood/infra/changes/1234

olivia: canary looks stable after keepalive patch + throttling. rolling to 100% and monitoring NAT port usage. Will file a short postmortem and add preventive tasks (egress proxy + S3 endpoints + alert runbook). :thumbsup:
